description: UsbDk (USB Development Kit): filter driver and library that give user-mode programs exclusive access to any USB device without replacing its driver. libusb uses it as a backend (MTKClient, QEMU, SPICE).
notes: Not portable: this runs the official MSI (UsbDk Runtime Libraries, Red Hat) into Program Files. It adds the
UsbDk filter driver to the USB stack and UsbDkHelper.dll to System32, where libusb looks for it.
Install, update and uninstall from an elevated (admin) shell. If the installer asks for a reboot, reboot.
x64 and x86 only: there is no ARM64 driver, and an x64 kernel driver cannot run on ARM64 Windows.
Upstream's last release is 1.0.22 from 17 March 2020. If a newer Windows refuses to load the driver
(e.g. Memory integrity), or USB devices misbehave, 'scoop uninstall UsbDk' removes it again.
Scoop links the install folder as 'UsbDk' inside its app folder; the command UsbDkController
(-n lists devices) comes from there. There is no window, so no shortcut in 'Scoop Apps'.
Only 'scoop uninstall UsbDk' removes the driver from the system.
A fresh install stops if UsbDk is already installed without Scoop. To let Scoop take over that copy,
run $env:GESU_ALLOW_EXISTING = '1' in the same shell and install again.
pre_install: if (!(is_admin)) { error "$app installs a driver: run this from an elevated shell."; break }
# Scoop falls back to the x64 package on ARM64, but a kernel driver must match the OS architecture.
if ([System.Runtime.InteropServices.RuntimeInformation]::OSArchitecture -eq 'Arm64') { error "$app has no ARM64 driver."; break }

script: $roots = 'HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Uninstall', 'HKLM:\SOFTWARE\WOW6432Node\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Uninstall'

$findEntry = { Get-ChildItem $roots -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Get-ItemProperty -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Where-Object { $_.DisplayName -eq 'UsbDk Runtime Libraries' -and $_.PSChildName -match '^\{[0-9A-Fa-f-]{36}\}$' } | Select-Object -First 1 }
# Do not adopt a copy installed outside Scoop, or 'scoop uninstall' would remove it; updates are fine.
if ($cmd -eq 'install' -and (& $findEntry) -and $env:GESU_ALLOW_EXISTING -ne '1') {
error "UsbDk is already installed without Scoop. Set `$env:GESU_ALLOW_EXISTING = '1' to let Scoop take it over."
break
# The MSI removes an older version itself (RemoveExistingProducts) and installs the driver with UsbDkInstHelper.
$proc = Start-Process msiexec.exe -ArgumentList @('/i', "`"$dir\setup.msi_`"", '/qn', '/norestart', '/l*v', "`"$dir\install.log`"") -Wait -PassThru
# 3010: installed, a reboot is needed to finish.
if ($proc.ExitCode -notin 0, 3010) { error "msiexec failed with exit code $($proc.ExitCode); see $($dir -replace [regex]::Escape($env:USERPROFILE), '%USERPROFILE%')\install.log."; break }
if ($proc.ExitCode -eq 3010) { warn 'Reboot to finish installing the UsbDk driver.' }
$installDir = (& $findEntry).InstallLocation
if (!$installDir) { $installDir = "$env:ProgramFiles\UsbDk Runtime Library" }
# Link the install folder into $dir, so that 'bin' (which Scoop resolves inside $dir) can point at it.

if (!(Test-Path "$installDir\UsbDkController.exe")) { warn "UsbDkController.exe was not found in $($installDir -replace [regex]::Escape($env:USERPROFILE), '%USERPROFILE%'); the command UsbDkController will not work."; return }
New-Item -ItemType Junction -Path "$dir\UsbDk" -Target $installDir.TrimEnd('\') | Out-Null
if (!(is_admin)) { error "$app removes a driver: run this from an elevated shell."; break }
# Remove only the junction to the install folder, never what it points to, before Scoop deletes $dir.
if (Test-Path "$dir\UsbDk") { [System.IO.Directory]::Delete("$dir\UsbDk") }
# On update the new MSI upgrades in place; only a real uninstall removes the driver.
if ($cmd -ne 'uninstall') { return }
$roots = 'HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Uninstall', 'HKLM:\SOFTWARE\WOW6432Node\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Uninstall'

$entry = Get-ChildItem $roots -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Get-ItemProperty -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Where-Object { $_.DisplayName -eq 'UsbDk Runtime Libraries' -and $_.PSChildName -match '^\{[0-9A-Fa-f-]{36}\}$' } | Select-Object -First 1
if (!$entry) { warn 'UsbDk was not found among installed programs; nothing to remove.'; return }
$proc = Start-Process msiexec.exe -ArgumentList @('/x', $entry.PSChildName, '/qn', '/norestart') -Wait -PassThru
if ($proc.ExitCode -notin 0, 3010) { warn "msiexec could not remove UsbDk (exit code $($proc.ExitCode)); remove 'UsbDk Runtime Libraries' in Apps." }
if ($proc.ExitCode -eq 3010) { warn 'Reboot to finish removing the UsbDk driver.' }
